Define a function with a custom vmap rule

Source: R/custom_batching.R
custom_vmap.Rd

Ports of jax.custom_batching.custom_vmap and sequential_vmap. A custom_vmap() function behaves like fun, except under vmap(), where vmap_rule is used.

Usage

custom_vmap(fun, vmap_rule = NULL)

custom_vmap_def_vmap(f, vmap_rule)

sequential_vmap(f)

Arguments

fun, f

A function. For custom_vmap_def_vmap(), a function created by custom_vmap().

vmap_rule

The vmap rule (can be set later with custom_vmap_def_vmap()).

Value

A function with a custom vmap rule.

Details

The rule is called as vmap_rule(axis_size, in_batched, ...): axis_size is the size of the mapped axis, in_batched is a list of logicals with the structure of the arguments saying which of them are batched, and ... are the arguments, with the mapped axis first in every batched one. It returns list(out, out_batched), where out_batched has the structure of out and says which outputs carry the mapped axis (first).

As in JAX, a custom_vmap() function supports forward mode differentiation but not reverse mode. To customize both, wrap the custom_vmap() function in custom_vjp(), with custom_vjp() on the outside.

sequential_vmap(f) is the special case whose rule calls f once per element in a loop (lax_map()), for functions that cannot handle a batch dimension.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f <- custom_vmap(function(x, y) x + y, function(axis_size, in_batched, xs, ys) {
  list(xs * ys, TRUE)
})
f(2, 3)                                           # 5
vmap(f)(jnp_arange(3L), jnp_arange(1L, 4L))       # 0 2 6: the rule multiplies

g <- sequential_vmap(function(x) x + 1)
vmap(g)(jnp_arange(3L))
} # }
